Dinamo Zagreb.q: Which English club did Dinamo Zagreb beat over two legs to win the 1967 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup?
Dinamo Zagreb.hint: Dinamo won 2-0 in Zagreb and drew 0-0 at Elland Road to take the tie 2-0 on aggregate — still the club's only European trophy.

Dinamo Zagreb.q: Dinamo Zagreb lost the 1963 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup final to which Spanish club?
Dinamo Zagreb.hint: Valencia won the competition in both 1962 and 1963; Dinamo went one better four years later against Leeds.

Dinamo Zagreb.q: Dinamo's 1967 Fairs Cup was the only European trophy won by a Yugoslav club until which side lifted the 1991 European Cup?
Dinamo Zagreb.hint: Red Star beat Marseille on penalties in Bari, 24 years after Dinamo's win. Partizan had lost the 1966 final.

Dinamo Zagreb.q: Which stadium has been Dinamo Zagreb's home ground?
Dinamo Zagreb.hint: Maksimir, in the east of Zagreb, takes its name from the park beside it.

Dinamo Zagreb.q: Who scored a hat-trick as Dinamo Zagreb beat Tottenham 3-0 to reach the 2021 Europa League quarter-finals?
Dinamo Zagreb.hint: Orsic's third came in extra time on 18 March 2021, overturning a 2-0 first-leg deficit for a 3-2 aggregate win — Dinamo's first European quarter-final.

Dinamo Zagreb.q: Which Dinamo Zagreb academy graduate joined Inter Milan in 2013 for around 11 million euros?
Dinamo Zagreb.hint: Kovacic was 19 when he left for Inter; Brozovic also joined Inter, but from Dinamo Zagreb's city rivals two years later.

Dinamo Zagreb.q: Which Dinamo Zagreb forward did Arsenal sign in 2007 for around 13.5 million euros?
Dinamo Zagreb.hint: The Brazilian-born Croatia international was Dinamo's second big 2007 sale — Corluka left in the same window, but for Manchester City.

Dinamo Zagreb.q: Which club did Mario Mandzukic join when he left Dinamo Zagreb in 2010?
Dinamo Zagreb.hint: Wolfsburg paid around 7 million euros; the move to Bayern Munich came two years later.

Dinamo Zagreb.q: Bosko Balaban's 7.8 million euro transfer from Dinamo Zagreb in 2001 took him to which English club?
Dinamo Zagreb.hint: It was a club-record sale at the time, though Balaban started only a handful of games at Villa Park.

Dinamo Zagreb.q: Which manager led Dinamo Zagreb through the 1966-67 season in which they won the Fairs Cup, before leaving that summer?
Dinamo Zagreb.hint: Zebec ran the campaign; Ivica Horvat took charge only for the two-legged final itself after Zebec's departure.

Hajduk Split.q: Hajduk Split's supporters' group Torcida, founded in 1950, holds which distinction?
o: The oldest organised supporters' group in Europe
The first group officially recognised by UEFA
The largest single supporters' group in Europe
The first to be granted a stand of their own
Hajduk Split.hint: Founded on 28 October 1950 by three students in Zagreb — Ante Doric, Ante Ivanisevic and Vjenceslav Zuvela.

Hajduk Split.q: Torcida, Hajduk Split's supporters' group, took its name from a fan movement in which country?
Hajduk Split.hint: The founders idolised the Brazilian torcida they had seen at the 1950 World Cup; the word comes from the Portuguese 'torcer'.

Hajduk Split.q: Torcida was founded the day before a decisive Hajduk Split fixture against which club?
Hajduk Split.hint: Hajduk won that match 2-1 on 29 October 1950, a day after the group was formed.

Hajduk Split.q: What made Hajduk Split's 1950 Yugoslav championship win remarkable?
o: They won it without losing a single match
They won it with an all-teenage side
They won it after starting the season with nine defeats
They won it while playing every game away
Hajduk Split.hint: An unbeaten Yugoslav title that no club matched in the 40 years before the league broke up.

Hajduk Split.q: Which stadium has been Hajduk Split's home since 1979?
Hajduk Split.hint: The 33,987-seat Poljud, with Torcida gathered in the north stand.

Hajduk Split.q: Along with Hajduk Split, Dinamo Zagreb and Red Star Belgrade, which club made up the 'Big Four' of Yugoslav football?
Hajduk Split.hint: The four dominated SFR Yugoslavia; Partizan also reached the 1966 European Cup final.

Hajduk Split.q: In which decade did Hajduk Split win Yugoslav league titles in 1950, 1952 and 1955?
